    <groupId>io.github.inference4j</groupId>
    <artifactId>inference4j-core</artifactId>
    <version>${inference4jVersion}</version>
    <exclusions>
        <exclusion>
            <groupId>com.microsoft.onnxruntime</groupId>
            <artifactId>onnxruntime</artifactId>
        </exclusion>
    </exclusions>
</dependency>
<dependency>
    <groupId>com.microsoft.onnxruntime</groupId>
    <artifactId>onnxruntime_gpu</artifactId>
    <version>${onnxruntimeVersion}</version>
</dependency>

Then enable CUDA in the builder:

try (var classifier = ResNetClassifier.builder()
        .sessionOptions(opts -> opts.addCUDA(0))  // device ID 0
        .build()) {
    classifier.classify(Path.of("cat.jpg"));
}

docs.title: Plugin execution providers
docs.text:
ONNX Runtime can also load execution providers from separately packaged plugin libraries, rather than only the ones compiled into the runtime. Microsoft ships several this way — the CUDA and WebGPU plugin EPs, for example — versioned independently of ONNX Runtime itself.

This is additive. addCoreML() and addCUDA() above are unaffected and remain the simplest path. Reach for a plugin EP when you need a backend that isn't built into your ONNX Runtime distribution.

docs.title: Register the plugin library
docs.text:
Registration happens on the OrtEnvironment, not on the session. inference4j uses ONNX Runtime's default environment, so anything you register there applies to every model you build afterwards:

OrtEnvironment env = OrtEnvironment.getEnvironment();
env.registerExecutionProviderLibrary("my_ep", "/path/to/plugin_ep_library.so");

docs.title: Pick devices and attach them
docs.text:
getEpDevices() lists every execution provider / device combination available, including ones contributed by registered plugins. Filter down to the provider you want, then pass the result to addExecutionProvider:

OrtEnvironment env = OrtEnvironment.getEnvironment();

List<OrtEpDevice> devices = env.getEpDevices().stream()
        .filter(d -> "my_ep".equals(d.getEpName()))
        .toList();

try (var classifier = ResNetClassifier.builder()
        .sessionOptions(opts -> opts.addExecutionProvider(devices, Map.of()))
        .build()) {
    classifier.classify(Path.of("cat.jpg"));
}

Two rules worth knowing:

  • Every OrtEpDevice in the list must belong to the same execution provider, though they may point at different devices.
  • Providers apply in the order added — the first provider added gets first choice when graph nodes are assigned.

docs.title: Inspect what's available
docs.text:
OrtEpDevice exposes getEpName(), getEpVendor(), getEpMetadata(), getEpOptions() and getDevice(), which is enough to see what a machine actually offers:

for (OrtEpDevice d : OrtEnvironment.getEnvironment().getEpDevices()) {
    System.out.println(d.getEpName() + " (" + d.getEpVendor() + ") -> " + d.getDevice());
}

To remove a plugin again:

env.unregisterExecutionProviderLibrary("my_ep");

Requires ONNX Runtime 1.24.3 or later

registerExecutionProviderLibrary(), getEpDevices() and addExecutionProvider() are not present in 1.23. inference4j depends on ONNX Runtime 1.28.0 as of 0.13.0, so they are available with no extra setup.

docs.title: The sessionOptions API
docs.text:
Every model wrapper exposes .sessionOptions(SessionConfigurer) in its builder. SessionConfigurer is a @FunctionalInterface that receives the ONNX Runtime SessionOptions:

@FunctionalInterface
public interface SessionConfigurer {
    void configure(OrtSession.SessionOptions options) throws OrtException;
}

This gives you full access to ONNX Runtime configuration:

.sessionOptions(opts -> {
    opts.addCoreML();
    opts.setIntraOpNumThreads(4);
})

docs.title: Common options
docs.text: Method Description opts.addCoreML() Enable CoreML (macOS) opts.addCUDA(deviceId) Enable CUDA (Linux/Windows) opts.addExecutionProvider(devices, options) Enable a plugin execution provider opts.setIntraOpNumThreads(n) Set number of threads for intra-op parallelism opts.setInterOpNumThreads(n) Set number of threads for inter-op parallelism opts.setOptimizationLevel(level) Set graph optimization level

docs.title: Benchmarks on Apple Silicon (M-series)
docs.text:
Model Capability CPU CoreML Speedup ResNet-50 Image Classification 37 ms 10 ms 3.7x CRAFT Text Detection 831 ms 153 ms 5.4x

Measured with 3 warmup runs + 10 timed runs.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• CoreML is available on macOS only. The addCoreML() call will fail on other platforms.
  • CUDA requires the onnxruntime_gpu artifact and a compatible NVIDIA driver + CUDA toolkit.
  • If the execution provider fails to initialize, ONNX Runtime silently falls back to CPU. Check logs for warnings.
  • For production workloads, benchmark both CPU and GPU — small models (like MiniLM) may be faster on CPU due to GPU data transfer overhead.
  • .sessionOptions() is composable — you can set multiple options in a single lambda.

docs.title: Model Loading
docs.text: inference4j resolves models through the ModelSource interface. By default, models are downloaded from HuggingFace and cached locally. You can also load models from disk or implement your own resolution strategy.

docs.title: ModelSource interface
docs.text:
@FunctionalInterface
public interface ModelSource {
    Path resolve(String modelId);

    // Defaults, overridden by HuggingFaceModelSource
    default ResolvedModel open(String modelId) { ... }
    default ResolvedModel open(String modelId, List<String> requiredFiles) { ... }
    default ResolvedModel open(String modelId, String subdirectory) { ... }
}

ModelSource takes a model ID and returns the local directory path where the model files live. Every builder accepts .modelSource(ModelSource).

Builders call open(...), which returns a ResolvedModel: the directory, plus a handle that keeps it in use until it is closed. For HuggingFaceModelSource, an open handle keeps the snapshot it points to on disk, so updates and pruning never delete files a model is loading or using. Lambdas and LocalModelSource return unmanaged handles, whose close() does nothing.

try (ResolvedModel model = source.open("inference4j/silero-vad", List.of("model.onnx"))) {
    InferenceSession session = InferenceSession.create(model, "model.onnx");
    // the session retains the snapshot until session.close()
}

docs.title: LocalModelSource
docs.text:
Load models from a directory on disk:

var source = new LocalModelSource(Path.of("/models"));

try (var classifier = DistilBertTextClassifier.builder()
        .modelId("my-sentiment-model")
        .modelSource(source)
        .build()) {
    classifier.classify("Great product!");
}

This resolves to /models/my-sentiment-model/, which should contain the model files (model.onnx, vocab.txt, config.json, etc.).

docs.title: HuggingFaceModelSource
docs.text:
The default model source. Downloads models from the HuggingFace Hub and caches them locally.

// Uses default cache directory (~/.cache/inference4j/)
var source = HuggingFaceModelSource.defaultInstance();

// Or specify a custom cache directory
var source = new HuggingFaceModelSource(Path.of("/custom/cache"));

// Or set every option
var source = HuggingFaceModelSource.builder()
        .cacheDir(Path.of("/custom/cache"))
        .checkInterval(Duration.ofHours(1))   // default: a day
        .offline(false)
        .endpoint(URI.create("https://hf-mirror.example.com"))
        .pruneMode(PruneMode.AUTO)                     // default; MANUAL keeps old snapshots
        .minimumSnapshotAge(Duration.ofMinutes(10))  // default
        .build();

docs.title: Cache layout
docs.text:
Each repo is cached as one or more snapshots, one per Hub commit:

~/.cache/inference4j/
  hub/
    .locks/models--inference4j--silero-vad.lock
    models--inference4j--silero-vad/
      refs/main                   the current snapshot's commit
      snapshots/{commit}/         the files at that commit
      manifests/{commit}.json     each file's Hub id and size
      repo.json                   the last update check

An update writes a new snapshot next to the current one and switches refs/main to it once every file is in place, so a model never reads files from two revisions. Files that did not change are reused, never downloaded again:

  • Moved from the old snapshot when no model in this JVM uses it and it is older than the minimum age. The update then only takes the space of the files that changed. The old snapshot keeps only its versions of the changed files, is never served again, and is pruned like any superseded snapshot.
  • Copied when a model in this JVM still uses the old snapshot, or the snapshot is younger than the minimum age, so that the running model keeps its files. An update while the old revision is in use needs disk space for both copies of the unchanged files until the old snapshot is pruned.

The cache never hard-links model files: ONNX Runtime refuses external data (model.onnx.data) that has more than one hard link. A snapshot file that has other hard links, as caches written by development builds before 0.15.0 have, is replaced by a private copy when it is opened, and a link back to the flat layout is removed instead (logged once per repo at INFO). Where the link count cannot be read, as on Windows, files are left as they are; a snapshot that a loaded model uses is left as it is too, with a warning.

resolve(...) returns the current snapshot's directory, such as ~/.cache/inference4j/hub/models--inference4j--silero-vad/snapshots/{commit}/. Code that built paths as {cacheDir}/{org}/{name}/ should use the returned path instead. A path from resolve is not protected from pruning; open returns a handle that is.

docs.title: Updates
docs.text:
Cached models stay in sync with the Hub. At most once per check interval (a day by default), opening a cached model asks the Hub for the repo's current revision, with one small API call.

  • Changed files are downloaded at the new commit into a new snapshot; unchanged files are moved or copied into it. A model card edit changes no cached file, so it creates no snapshot and downloads nothing; the check is recorded in repo.json.
  • Files requested between checks, such as a file a second wrapper needs from the same repo, are downloaded at the commit of the current snapshot, never at the Hub's latest.
  • Models already loaded keep reading the snapshot they were loaded from. Models loaded afterwards read the new one.
  • Hub unreachable: if the check fails (no network, timeout, an error response), the cached files are used and a warning is logged once. If a download fails during an update, the current snapshot stays in use, a warning is logged, and the next check resumes the update without downloading again the files already fetched.
  • Revision API unavailable but downloads working: missing files are downloaded, and the snapshot is named after the commit the Hub reports with the download (X-Repo-Commit), or unknown without it.
  • Offline mode never contacts the Hub: cached files are used as they are, and a model that is not fully cached fails to load. Turn it on with INFERENCE4J_OFFLINE=true, -Dinference4j.offline=true, HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 or .offline(true).
  • Check interval: INFERENCE4J_CACHE_CHECK_INTERVAL or -Dinference4j.cache.check-interval take an ISO-8601 duration, such as PT1H or P7D; PT0S checks on every load.
  • Mirrors: HF_ENDPOINT or -Dinference4j.hf.endpoint point to a Hub mirror.

docs.title: Caches from earlier versions
docs.text:
Versions before 0.15.0 cached files flat, in {cacheDir}/{org}/{name}/. These caches are adopted the first time each repo is opened, without downloading again:

  • Online: each cached file is hashed once and compared with the Hub's id. Files that match are moved into the new snapshot; files that differ are downloaded.
  • Offline: the files are moved into a snapshot named unknown, and checked against the Hub at the next online open, which promotes them to a snapshot named after the Hub's commit.
  • Adopted files leave the flat layout, so they take no extra disk space. An older inference4j version sharing the cache no longer finds them there and downloads them again. Where a file cannot be moved (another file system), it is copied and the flat file deleted. ModelCache.prune() deletes flat files left at the paths of adopted ones.
  • Read-only cache: when the cache directory cannot be written, cached files (flat or snapshot) are read in place, without update checks or eviction protection, and a warning is logged once.

docs.title: Managing the cache
docs.text:
HuggingFaceModelSource.cache() returns a ModelCache, and ModelCache.defaultCache() is the default source's:

ModelCache cache = ModelCache.defaultCache();

for (CachedModel model : cache.list()) {          // local state only
    System.out.printf("%s %s %d bytes%n", model.repoId(), model.revision(), model.sizeBytes());
}

UpdateCheck check = cache.check("inference4j/silero-vad");   // asks the Hub, downloads nothing
if (check.updateAvailable()) {
    cache.update("inference4j/silero-vad");                  // downloads the changed files now
}

cache.evict("inference4j/silero-vad");            // deletes the repo's snapshots not in use
cache.prune();                                    // deletes superseded snapshots of every repo
Method Description list() Every cached repo: current revision, last check, remote revision, snapshots, files, leases and size. Reads local state only. find(repoId) One cached repo, or empty. check(repoId) Asks the Hub which cached files changed, without downloading. The result is recorded, so the next load fetches them. update(repoId) Brings the repo up to date now, whatever the check interval. evict(repoId) Deletes the repo's snapshots that are not in use, and its adopted flat files. evict(repoId, revision) Deletes one snapshot, unless it is in use. prune() Deletes superseded snapshots that are not in use, unfinished downloads, and adopted flat files, in every repo.

CachedModel.stale() is true when a model still loaded in this JVM reads an older snapshot whose files differ from the current one: it serves an older version of the model than a model loaded now would. Evictions return an EvictionResult with the snapshots removed, those kept because they are in use, and the bytes freed (a file still hard-linked from a kept snapshot, as by development builds before 0.15.0, does not count).

In a Spring Boot application, the starter's models actuator endpoint offers these operations over HTTP, and its health indicator reports stale models and available updates.

docs.title: Pruning and snapshots in use
docs.text:
A snapshot is in use while a handle on it is open: a builder holds one while it loads, and each InferenceSession (and each genai model) created from it holds its own until it is closed. Pruning and eviction skip snapshots in use.

  • Pruning mode: with auto (the default), the snapshots an update supersedes are deleted right after it, unless they are in use. With manual, they stay until prune() or evict(...). Set it with -Dinference4j.cache.prune=manual, INFERENCE4J_CACHE_PRUNE=manual or .pruneMode(PruneMode.MANUAL).
  • Minimum age: leases are counted in the JVM only, so a snapshot another process sharing the cache is still loading cannot be seen as in use. Pruning and eviction therefore never delete a snapshot younger than the minimum age, 10 minutes by default, counted from its creation. Set it with .minimumSnapshotAge(Duration).
  • Other processes: a process that loaded an older snapshot and keeps running is not protected once that snapshot is past the minimum age: an update may move its unchanged files into the new snapshot, and pruning may delete it. On Linux and macOS, files moved or deleted while open (such as memory-mapped external weights in model.onnx.data) stay readable until closed; single-file models are read into memory when the session is built. On Windows, a snapshot with open files cannot be deleted; it is reported as in use and left for a later prune.
  • Locking: updates, adoption and eviction of a repo run under an exclusive lock file in hub/.locks/, so two processes never download the same repo at once; one waits for the other. File locks are not reliable on network file systems (NFS, SMB); give each host its own cache directory there.

docs.title: Cache directory resolution
docs.text:
The cache directory is resolved in this order:

  1. Constructor parameter (new HuggingFaceModelSource(path))
  2. System property: -Dinference4j.cache.dir=/path/to/cache
  3. Environment variable: INFERENCE4J_CACHE_DIR=/path/to/cache
  4. Default: ~/.cache/inference4j/

docs.title: Downloaded files
docs.text:
HuggingFaceModelSource attempts to download these files (skipping any that don't exist):

  • model.onnx — the ONNX model
  • vocab.txt — WordPiece vocabulary (NLP models)
  • vocab.json — JSON vocabulary (audio models)
  • config.json — HuggingFace model config
  • labels.txt — class labels (vision models)

docs.title: Lambda shorthand
docs.text:
Since ModelSource is a @FunctionalInterface, you can use a lambda:

try (var classifier = ResNetClassifier.builder()
        .modelId("resnet50")
        .modelSource(id -> Path.of("/models").resolve(id))
        .build()) {
    classifier.classify(Path.of("cat.jpg"));
}

docs.title: Required model files by task
docs.text: Task Required files Text classification model.onnx, vocab.txt, config.json (with id2label) Text embeddings model.onnx, vocab.txt Search reranking model.onnx, vocab.txt Image classification model.onnx, labels.txt Object detection model.onnx, labels.txt Text detection model.onnx Speech-to-text model.onnx, vocab.json Voice activity detection model.onnx

docs.title: Using a custom HuggingFace model
docs.text:
Any ONNX-exported model hosted on HuggingFace works — just override the model ID:

try (var classifier = DistilBertTextClassifier.builder()
        .modelId("your-org/your-fine-tuned-model")
        .build()) {
    classifier.classify("Some text");
}

The model repository must contain the required files listed above.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• LocalModelSource does no downloading — it expects files to already exist at the resolved path.
  • HuggingFaceModelSource is thread-safe. Concurrent requests for the same model wait for the first download to complete. Sources on the same cache directory share their locks and leases.
  • Cached models are checked for updates once a day (see Updates). To force a full re-download, call cache().evict(repoId) once no model uses the repo.
  • The model ID is just a string — it can be any identifier meaningful to your ModelSource implementation.

docs.title: Spring Boot
docs.text: inference4j provides a Spring Boot starter with opt-in auto-configuration for all supported models.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Spring Boot 4.0 or later Spring Framework 7.0 or later Java 17 or later

Spring Boot 4 required as of inference4j 0.11.0

The starter targets Spring Boot 4. It will not load in a Spring Boot 3 application — Boot 4 relocated the actuator health types, so the two lines are binary-incompatible and cannot be served by one artifact.

If you are still on Spring Boot 3, stay on inference4j-spring-boot-starter:0.10.1, which is the last release built against Boot 3.4. It is frozen, not maintained — Spring Boot 3.x itself left open-source support on 30 June 2026, so migrating to Boot 4 is the recommended path. See Migrating from 0.10.x below.

Only the starter is affected. inference4j-core and every other module are plain Java libraries with no Spring dependency, and work unchanged on any Spring version or none at all.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Add the starter dependency:

GradleMaven 
implementation 'io.github.inference4j:inference4j-spring-boot-starter:${inference4jVersion}'

<dependency>
    <groupId>io.github.inference4j</groupId>
    <artifactId>inference4j-spring-boot-starter</artifactId>
    <version>${inference4jVersion}</version>
</dependency>

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Every model is opt-in — nothing is downloaded until you set enabled: true.

inference4j:
  nlp:
    text-classifier:
      enabled: true

docs.title: All properties
docs.text: Property Type Default Description inference4j.actuator.models.enabled boolean true Create the models actuator endpoint bean when Spring Boot Actuator is on the classpath. It still has to be exposed with management.endpoints.web.exposure.include inference4j.dashboard.enabled boolean false Serve the dashboard in a Spring MVC web application inference4j.dashboard.path String /inference4j The path the dashboard is served at; its JSON API is under <path>/api inference4j.dashboard.read-only boolean true When false, the dashboard can update, evict and prune cached models inference4j.health.model-cache-ttl Duration 10s How long the health indicator reuses its listing of the model cache (staleModels, updatesAvailable), so frequent probes don't read the cache each time. 0s lists it on every call inference4j.metrics.enabled boolean true Use a Micrometer-backed RouterMetrics when a MeterRegistry is present. When false, or when Micrometer is absent, RouterMetrics falls back to a no-op instead of being removed inference4j.nlp.text-classifier.enabled boolean false Enable DistilBERT text classifier inference4j.nlp.text-classifier.model-id String inference4j/distilbert-base-uncased-finetuned-sst-2-english Model ID inference4j.nlp.text-embedder.enabled boolean false Enable SentenceTransformer embedder inference4j.nlp.text-embedder.model-id String (required) Model ID (no default — must be specified) inference4j.nlp.search-reranker.enabled boolean false Enable MiniLM cross-encoder reranker inference4j.nlp.search-reranker.model-id String inference4j/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2 Model ID inference4j.nlp.named-entity-recognizer.enabled boolean false Enable BERT NER recognizer inference4j.nlp.named-entity-recognizer.model-id String inference4j/distilbert-NER Model ID inference4j.vision.image-classifier.enabled boolean false Enable ResNet image classifier inference4j.vision.image-classifier.model-id String inference4j/resnet50-v1-7 Model ID inference4j.vision.object-detector.enabled boolean false Enable the object detector inference4j.vision.object-detector.architecture String detr Wrapper that builds the bean: detr (DetrDetector), yolov8 (YoloV8Detector) or yolo26 (Yolo26Detector). See Object detection inference4j.vision.object-detector.model-id String the architecture's default Model ID. Unset, it is inference4j/dfine-small-coco for detr, inference4j/yolov8n for yolov8 and inference4j/yolo26n for yolo26 inference4j.vision.pose-detector.enabled boolean false Enable the pose detector (RtmoPoseDetector) inference4j.vision.pose-detector.model-id String inference4j/rtmo-s-coco Model ID: inference4j/rtmo-m-coco, inference4j/rtmo-l-coco, or your own RTMO weights inference4j.vision.pose-detector.confidence-threshold float 0.5 Lowest person score a pose is returned for inference4j.vision.text-detector.enabled boolean false Enable CRAFT text detector inference4j.vision.text-detector.model-id String inference4j/craft-mlt-25k Model ID inference4j.audio.speech-recognizer.enabled boolean false Enable Wav2Vec2 speech recognizer inference4j.audio.speech-recognizer.model-id String inference4j/wav2vec2-base-960h Model ID inference4j.audio.vad.enabled boolean false Enable Silero VAD inference4j.audio.vad.model-id String inference4j/silero-vad Model ID inference4j.genai.text-generator.enabled boolean false Enable the onnxruntime-genai TextGenerator (requires inference4j-genai) inference4j.genai.text-generator.model String phi-3-mini Preset: phi-3-mini, phi-4-mini, deepseek-r1-1.5b, qwen3-0.6b or smollm3-3b inference4j.genai.text-generator.max-length / temperature / top-k / top-p number builder defaults Generation settings; unset keeps the builder's default inference4j.genai.vision-language.enabled boolean false Enable VisionLanguageModel (requires inference4j-genai) inference4j.genai.vision-language.model String phi-3.5-vision Preset: phi-3.5-vision inference4j.genai.vision-language.max-length / temperature / top-k / top-p number builder defaults Generation settings inference4j.genai.whisper.enabled boolean false Enable WhisperSpeechModel; it also becomes the SpeechRecognizer bean (requires inference4j-genai) inference4j.genai.whisper.model-id String inference4j/whisper-small-genai Model ID (inference4j/whisper-tiny-genai for the small, fast one) inference4j.genai.whisper.language String en Source language code inference4j.genai.whisper.task String transcribe transcribe or translate (to English) inference4j.genai.whisper.max-length int 448 Maximum tokens per 30-second chunk

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Beans are registered by their interface type, so you inject the interface — not the concrete implementation:

@RestController
public class SentimentController {
    private final TextClassifier classifier;

    public SentimentController(TextClassifier classifier) {
        this.classifier = classifier;
    }

    @PostMapping("/analyze")
    public List<TextClassification> analyze(@RequestBody String text) {
        return classifier.classify(text);
    }
}

docs.title: Object detection
docs.text:
inference4j.vision.object-detector.enabled=true registers an ObjectDetector built with DetrDetector and D-FINE small (inference4j/dfine-small-coco, Apache-2.0 weights). Its default confidence threshold is 0.5.

To use a YOLO model, set architecture. Without a model-id, each architecture loads its own default model, so the D-FINE weights are never handed to a YOLO wrapper:

inference4j:
  vision:
    object-detector:
      enabled: true
      architecture: yolov8          # loads inference4j/yolov8n (AGPL-3.0 weights)

A model-id must match the architecture: other DETR-family models such as inference4j/dfine-nano-coco or inference4j/rtdetr-v2-r18vd work with detr, and a YOLOv8 checkpoint needs architecture: yolov8.

Changed in 0.15.0

Before 0.15.0 the bean was always YoloV8Detector with inference4j/yolov8n and a confidence threshold of 0.25. Applications that set a YOLO model-id must now also set architecture, or the model is loaded by DetrDetector.

docs.title: Pose detection
docs.text:
inference4j.vision.pose-detector.enabled=true registers a PoseDetector built with RtmoPoseDetector and RTMO-s trained on COCO only (inference4j/rtmo-s-coco). Pick a larger model with model-id:

inference4j:
  vision:
    pose-detector:
      enabled: true
      model-id: inference4j/rtmo-m-coco
      confidence-threshold: 0.6

@RestController
public class PoseController {
    private final PoseDetector detector;

    public PoseController(PoseDetector detector) {
        this.detector = detector;
    }

    @PostMapping("/poses")
    public List<Pose> poses(@RequestParam MultipartFile image) throws IOException {
        return detector.detect(ImageIO.read(image.getInputStream()));
    }
}

See Pose detection.

docs.title: Generative models
docs.text:
Add inference4j-genai next to the starter, and the text generator, vision-language model and Whisper become available with the same opt-in properties:

inference4j:
  genai:
    text-generator:
      enabled: true
      model: phi-3-mini
      max-length: 512
    whisper:
      enabled: true
      model-id: inference4j/whisper-tiny-genai

public AssistantController(TextGenerator generator, SpeechRecognizer recognizer) { … }

Without inference4j-genai on the classpath, the inference4j.genai.* properties are ignored.

WhisperSpeechModel is a SpeechRecognizer, so with inference4j.genai.whisper.enabled=true it replaces Wav2Vec2 as the application's SpeechRecognizer bean, even if inference4j.audio.speech-recognizer.enabled is also set. Inject WhisperSpeechModel directly for Whisper-only options. For recordings longer than 30 seconds, wrap it yourself in a SegmentedSpeechRecognizer bean.

Presets cover the models with known chat templates. For any other genai model, define your own TextGenerator bean with modelSource and chatTemplate; it replaces the auto-configured one.

docs.title: Overriding beans
docs.text:
All auto-configured beans use @ConditionalOnMissingBean, so you can replace any model with your own implementation:

@Configuration
public class CustomModelConfig {

    @Bean
    public TextClassifier textClassifier() {
        return DistilBertTextClassifier.builder()
            .modelId("your-org/your-model")
            .sessionOptions(opts -> opts.addCoreML())
            .build();
    }
}

When you define your own bean, the auto-configured one is skipped.

docs.title: Health indicator
docs.text:
An actuator health indicator is included automatically when Spring Boot Actuator is on the classpath. It reports the number of registered InferenceTask and GenerativeTask beans (a bean that is both, like WhisperSpeechModel, counts once).

GET /actuator/health

{
  "status": "UP",
  "components": {
    "inference4j": {
      "status": "UP",
      "details": {
        "tasks": 3,
        "staleModels": [
          {
            "repo": "inference4j/silero-vad",
            "loadedRevisions": ["3f1c..."],
            "cachedRevision": "9a7e..."
          }
        ],
        "updatesAvailable": ["inference4j/distilbert-NER"]
      }
    }
  }
}

The two model cache details come from the model cache on disk, without calling the Hub:

Detail Description staleModels Repos where a model loaded in this JVM reads an older snapshot whose files differ from the cached revision, so it serves an older version than a model loaded now would. loadedRevisions are the snapshots still in use. updatesAvailable Repos whose last Hub check found changed files that are not downloaded yet.

Neither changes the status: a stale model still serves requests. Restarting the application, or rebuilding the model bean, loads the cached revision. The details appear when a ModelCache bean exists, which the starter defines by default.

The health indicator is enabled by default. Disable it with:

inference4j:
  health:
    enabled: false

docs.title: Model cache endpoint
docs.text:
With Spring Boot Actuator on the classpath, the starter adds a models endpoint over the model cache: it lists the cached models, checks them for updates, and can update, evict and prune them. Like most actuator endpoints, it is not exposed over HTTP until you include it:

management:
  endpoints:
    web:
      exposure:
        include: health,models

docs.title: Operations
docs.text:
Request Access Description Status GET /actuator/models read Every cached repo: revision, last check, snapshots, files, leases, size, stale, updating. Local state only. 200 GET /actuator/models/{org}/{name} read One cached repo. 200, 404 when not cached GET /actuator/models/{org}/{name}?check=true read Also asks the Hub which cached files changed, without downloading. A check younger than a minute is reused. 200, 404, 409 offline, 502 Hub unreachable POST /actuator/models/{org}/{name} with {"action":"update"} write Starts an update in the background: downloads the changed files into a new snapshot. 202, 400 unknown action, 404 DELETE /actuator/models/{org}/{name} write Evicts the repo: deletes its snapshots that are not in use. 200, 404 DELETE /actuator/models/{org}/{name}?revision={commit} write Deletes one snapshot, unless it is in use. 200, 404 DELETE /actuator/models write Prunes every repo: deletes superseded snapshots that are not in use, and unfinished downloads. 200

An invalid repo id or revision answers 400. Errors have a JSON body with status and message. Responses list paths inside the repo only, never the cache directory.

# every cached model
curl http://localhost:8080/actuator/models

# one model, asking the Hub whether it changed
curl 'http://localhost:8080/actuator/models/inference4j/silero-vad?check=true'

{
  "repoId": "inference4j/silero-vad",
  "revision": "9a7e...",
  "lastChecked": "2026-11-22T10:00:00Z",
  "remoteRevision": "b21d...",
  "updateAvailable": true,
  "stale": false,
  "updating": false,
  "snapshots": [
    {
      "revision": "9a7e...",
      "current": true,
      "leases": 1,
      "files": [{ "path": "model.onnx", "id": "4c5f...", "sizeBytes": 2313101 }],
      "sizeBytes": 2313101
    }
  ],
  "sizeBytes": 2313101,
  "check": {
    "cachedRevision": "9a7e...",
    "remoteRevision": "b21d...",
    "changedFiles": ["model.onnx"],
    "checkedAt": "2026-11-22T10:00:00Z",
    "updateAvailable": true
  }
}

The write operations, once enabled:

# update in the background; GET the model to follow it ("updating", then the new "revision")
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/actuator/models/inference4j/silero-vad \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"action":"update"}'

# evict a model, or one of its snapshots
curl -X DELETE http://localhost:8080/actuator/models/inference4j/silero-vad
curl -X DELETE 'http://localhost:8080/actuator/models/inference4j/silero-vad?revision=9a7e...'

# prune every repo
curl -X DELETE http://localhost:8080/actuator/models

Updates run one at a time, on a thread the endpoint owns. A request for a repo whose update is already running answers 202 with "status": "already-running". A failed update is logged as a warning, and the repo keeps its current snapshot. Models already loaded keep reading their snapshot after an update; models loaded afterwards read the new one. An eviction keeps the snapshots in use, listed under inUse in the response.

docs.title: Enabling writes
docs.text:
The endpoint's default access is read-only: POST and DELETE are not mapped, and answer 405. To allow them:

management:
  endpoint:
    models:
      access: unrestricted

management.endpoints.access.max-permitted caps this setting, as for every endpoint.

docs.title: Path
docs.text:
The URL follows the actuator base path and can be moved like any endpoint's:

management:
  endpoints:
    web:
      path-mapping:
        models: model-cache      # /actuator/model-cache

docs.title: Disabling the endpoint
docs.text:
Leaving models out of the exposure list keeps it off HTTP. To not create the bean at all, for example to define your own endpoint with the id models over the ModelCache bean:

inference4j:
  actuator:
    models:
      enabled: false

management.endpoint.models.access: none also removes it.

docs.title: Which cache
docs.text: The endpoint and the health details use the ModelCache bean. By default it is the cache of your HuggingFaceModelSource bean when you define one, and otherwise ModelCache.defaultCache(), the cache the auto-configured models download into. Define a ModelCache bean to use another one.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• The endpoint is not exposed over HTTP by default.
  • ?check=true makes an outbound request to the Hub (or the mirror in HF_ENDPOINT). It runs only for repos already cached, so a request cannot make the application contact the Hub about an arbitrary repo id.
  • The write operations can fill the disk (update downloads files) or force the next model loads to download again (DELETE). When you enable them, put the endpoint behind authentication, and keep CSRF protection on for POST and DELETE, for example with Spring Security's EndpointRequest.to("models") matcher.
  • update pulls the latest commit of the repo's main branch. It does not pin a revision.

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text:
The starter can serve a local dashboard, a web page over the model cache. It shows the cache's size and the disk usage of its volume, the largest models, and every cached repo with its snapshots and files. When writes are enabled, it can also check repos for updates, update, evict and prune them.

The dashboard needs a Spring MVC web application (spring-boot-starter-webmvc) and is off by default:

inference4j:
  dashboard:
    enabled: true
    read-only: false     # allow update, evict and prune; checking for updates is always allowed

It is served at http://localhost:8080/inference4j/, and the URL is logged at startup. Its page, styles and scripts ship in inference4j-core; there are no requests to a CDN, so it also works offline. It uses the same ModelCacheService bean as the model cache endpoint, so updates started from either one show as updating in both.

The page reads a small JSON API, which other tools can call too:

Request Description Status GET /inference4j/api/info {"readOnly": true} 200 GET /inference4j/api/cache The cache summary: models, snapshots, sizes, and the volume's disk.totalBytes and disk.usableBytes 200 GET /inference4j/api/cache/models Every cached repo 200 GET /inference4j/api/cache/model?repo={org}/{name}[&check=true] One cached repo; with check, after asking the Hub 200, 400, 404, 409 offline, 502 Hub unreachable POST /inference4j/api/cache/update?repo={org}/{name} Starts an update in the background 202, 403 read-only, 404 DELETE /inference4j/api/cache/model?repo={org}/{name}[&revision={commit}] Evicts the repo, or one snapshot 200, 403, 404 POST /inference4j/api/cache/prune Prunes superseded snapshots not in use 200, 403

docs.title: Dashboard security
docs.text:
• The dashboard has no authentication of its own. It is meant for local development; in a deployed application, leave it off or put its path behind your Spring Security configuration.
  • Like the endpoint's ?check=true, a check runs only for repos already cached.
  • With Spring Security's cookie CSRF repository (CookieCsrfTokenRepository), the page sends the XSRF-TOKEN cookie back as the X-XSRF-TOKEN header on POST and DELETE.

docs.title: Example configuration
docs.text:
A typical production setup enabling sentiment analysis and semantic search:

inference4j:
  nlp:
    text-classifier:
      enabled: true
    text-embedder:
      enabled: true
      model-id: inference4j/all-MiniLM-L6-v2
    search-reranker:
      enabled: true

@Service
public class SearchService {
    private final TextEmbedder embedder;
    private final SearchReranker reranker;

    public SearchService(TextEmbedder embedder, SearchReranker reranker) {
        this.embedder = embedder;
        this.reranker = reranker;
    }

    public List<SearchResult> search(String query, List<String> candidates) {
        // Stage 1: embed and retrieve
        float[] queryEmb = embedder.encode(query);
        // ... cosine similarity ranking ...

        // Stage 2: rerank top candidates
        float[] scores = reranker.scoreBatch(query, topCandidates);
        // ... sort by score ...
        return results;
    }
}

docs.title: Lazy loading
docs.text:
All inference4j beans are lazy by default — models are downloaded and ONNX sessions are created on first use, not at application startup. This keeps startup fast even when multiple models are enabled.

The trade-off is that the first request to each model may be slower due to the model download and session initialization.

docs.title: Warming up specific models
docs.text:
If you need a model ready immediately (e.g., for latency-sensitive endpoints), inject it eagerly at startup with an ApplicationReadyEvent listener:

@Component
public class ModelWarmup {
    private final TextClassifier classifier;

    public ModelWarmup(TextClassifier classifier) {
        this.classifier = classifier;
    }

    @EventListener(ApplicationReadyEvent.class)
    public void warmup() {
        classifier.classify("warmup");
    }
}

This triggers the lazy bean initialization during startup, so the model is ready when the first real request arrives.

docs.title: Migrating from 0.10.x
docs.text:
inference4j 0.11.0 moved the starter from Spring Boot 3 to Spring Boot 4. There is no Boot 3 branch — 0.10.1 is the last Boot 3 release and stays available on Maven Central.

1. Upgrade your application to Spring Boot 4. Spring's own migration guide recommends going to 3.5 first, then to 4.0. Boot 4 requires Java 17 or later.

2. Update the health indicator import, if you override it. The actuator health types moved modules in Boot 4. If you replace inference4j's default indicator with your own bean, change:

// Before (Spring Boot 3)
import org.springframework.boot.actuate.health.Health;
import org.springframework.boot.actuate.health.HealthIndicator;

// After (Spring Boot 4)
import org.springframework.boot.health.contributor.Health;
import org.springframework.boot.health.contributor.HealthIndicator;

The interface itself is unchanged — HealthIndicator is still a @FunctionalInterface returning Health, so an existing lambda keeps working once the import is fixed.

3. Nothing else changes. Every inference4j.* property, bean name and default is identical to 0.10.x. If you do not override the health indicator, upgrading your Boot version is the only step.

docs.title: If you cannot move to Spring Boot 4 yet
docs.text:
Pin the starter to the last Boot 3 release and let it float independently of the rest:

GradleMaven 
implementation 'io.github.inference4j:inference4j-spring-boot-starter:0.10.1'
implementation 'io.github.inference4j:inference4j-core:${inference4jVersion}'

<dependency>
    <groupId>io.github.inference4j</groupId>
    <artifactId>inference4j-spring-boot-starter</artifactId>
    <version>0.10.1</version>
</dependency>
<dependency>
    <groupId>io.github.inference4j</groupId>
    <artifactId>inference4j-core</artifactId>
    <version>${inference4jVersion}</version>
</dependency>

inference4j-core has no Spring dependency, so you can keep it current while the starter stays pinned. The 0.10.1 starter will not receive fixes.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Use model-id to swap models without changing code (e.g., switch from ResNet to EfficientNet).
  • The text embedder has no default model ID — you must specify one via model-id.
  • All beans implement AutoCloseable and are properly cleaned up on application shutdown.

docs.title: Tokenizers
docs.text:
Transformer models don't work with raw text — they expect sequences of integer token IDs mapped from a fixed vocabulary. A tokenizer bridges this gap: it splits text into tokens, maps each token to its vocabulary index, and produces the metadata tensors (attention_mask, token_type_ids) that the model expects as input.

inference4j handles tokenization automatically. When you call classifier.classify("some text"), the wrapper tokenizes the input, runs inference, and decodes the output — you never touch a token ID. But if you need to customize tokenization or use tokenizers directly, this guide covers how.

docs.title: Built-in tokenizers
docs.text:
inference4j ships five tokenizer implementations, covering the most common algorithms in production transformer models:

Tokenizer Algorithm Models Vocabulary format WordPieceTokenizer WordPiece (greedy longest-match subword splitting) BERT, DistilBERT, MiniLM, SentenceTransformer vocab.txt (one token per line) BpeTokenizer Byte-level BPE (iterative pair merging) CLIP vocab.json + merges.txt DecodingBpeTokenizer Byte-level BPE with decode support GPT-2, SmolLM2, Qwen2.5, BART vocab.json + merges.txt SentencePieceBpeTokenizer SentencePiece BPE (Unicode-native, ▁ space prefix) Gemma, LLaMA, TinyLlama, MarianMT tokenizer.json UnigramTokenizer SentencePiece Unigram (Viterbi optimal segmentation) Flan-T5, CoEdIT, T5SqlGenerator tokenizer.json

docs.title: WordPiece
docs.text:
WordPiece breaks unknown words into known subword units using a ## continuation prefix. For example, "unbelievable" becomes ["un", "##believ", "##able"] — preserving meaning even for out-of-vocabulary words.

The encoding pipeline:

  1. Lowercase and split on whitespace/punctuation
  2. Split each word into subwords via greedy longest-match against the vocabulary
  3. Wrap with [CLS] and [SEP] special tokens
  4. Truncate to maxLength if needed
Tokenizer tokenizer = WordPieceTokenizer.fromVocabFile(Path.of("vocab.txt"));
EncodedInput encoded = tokenizer.encode("Hello world!", 128);
// encoded.inputIds()      → [101, 7592, 2088, 999, 102]
// encoded.attentionMask() → [1, 1, 1, 1, 1]
// encoded.tokenTypeIds()  → [0, 0, 0, 0, 0]

WordPiece also supports sentence pair encoding for cross-encoder models (e.g., rerankers):

EncodedInput encoded = tokenizer.encode("What is Java?", "Java is a programming language.", 128);
// Format: [CLS] textA [SEP] textB [SEP]
// tokenTypeIds: 0 for textA tokens, 1 for textB tokens

Note

The built-in WordPieceTokenizer applies unconditional lowercasing, matching bert-base-uncased and distilbert-base-uncased. It is not suitable for cased models.

docs.title: Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE)
docs.text:
BPE starts from individual characters and iteratively merges the most frequent pairs into subwords. CLIP's variant adds byte-level encoding (handling any UTF-8 input) and </w> end-of-word markers.

The encoding pipeline:

  1. Lowercase and normalize whitespace
  2. Split via regex into words, contractions, digits, and punctuation
  3. Encode each byte via GPT-2's byte-to-unicode table
  4. Apply BPE merges according to the priority table
  5. Wrap with <|startoftext|> and <|endoftext|> special tokens
  6. Pad to maxLength (default: 77 for CLIP)
Tokenizer tokenizer = BpeTokenizer.fromFiles(
        Path.of("vocab.json"), Path.of("merges.txt"));
EncodedInput encoded = tokenizer.encode("a photo of a cat");
// encoded.inputIds()      → [49406, 320, 1125, 539, 320, 2368, 49407, 0, ...]
// encoded.attentionMask() → [1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 0, ...]

docs.title: Decoding BPE
docs.text:
DecodingBpeTokenizer extends BpeTokenizer with the ability to decode token IDs back to text. This is required by generative models that produce token IDs as output — autoregressive (GPT-2, SmolLM2, Qwen2.5) and encoder-decoder (BART).

The encoding pipeline is the same as BPE. The decoding pipeline:

  1. Reverse vocabulary lookup (ID → token string)
  2. Concatenate tokens
  3. Decode GPT-2 byte-to-unicode mapping back to raw bytes
  4. Interpret bytes as UTF-8
DecodingBpeTokenizer tokenizer = DecodingBpeTokenizer.fromFiles(
        Path.of("vocab.json"), Path.of("merges.txt"));

// Encode
EncodedInput encoded = tokenizer.encode("Hello world");

// Decode
String text = tokenizer.decode(new int[]{15496, 995}); // "Hello world"

// Streaming: one TokenStream per generation, fed token by token
TokenStream stream = tokenizer.newStream();
String fragment = stream.next(15496); // "Hello"
String rest = stream.flush();         // bytes still held at the end, if any

A character can span several tokens (byte-level BPE and <0xNN> byte tokens split UTF-8). A TokenStream holds those bytes until the character is complete, so next returns "" in the meantime. The tokenizer itself is thread-safe, but each stream is not: open one per generation and use it from one thread.

docs.title: SentencePiece BPE
docs.text:
SentencePiece BPE operates directly on Unicode text without a pre-tokenization regex. Word boundaries are encoded using the ▁ (U+2581) space prefix, and characters not in the vocabulary fall back to <0xNN> byte tokens.

The encoding pipeline:

  1. Prepend ▁ and replace all spaces with ▁
  2. Split on special tokens (added tokens preserved atomically)
  3. Split into characters and apply BPE merges
  4. Characters not in vocab → UTF-8 bytes → <0xNN> token IDs

SentencePieceBpeTokenizer is used automatically by OnnxTextGenerator.tinyLlama(), OnnxTextGenerator.gemma2(), and MarianTranslator. For custom SentencePiece models, use the TokenizerProvider:

try (var gen = OnnxTextGenerator.builder()
        .modelId("my-org/my-sentencepiece-model")
        .tokenizerProvider(SentencePieceBpeTokenizer.provider())
        .chatTemplate(msg -> "<start>" + msg + "<end>")
        .build()) {
    gen.generate("Hello", token -> System.out.print(token));
}

docs.title: Unigram
docs.text:
The Unigram algorithm assigns a log-probability score to every token in the vocabulary and uses dynamic programming (Viterbi) to find the segmentation that maximizes the total score. This is used by T5-family models (Flan-T5, CoEdIT, T5SqlGenerator).

The encoding pipeline:

  1. Prepend ▁ and replace all spaces with ▁
  2. Split on added tokens (special tokens preserved atomically)
  3. Run Viterbi to find the optimal segmentation
  4. Unmapped characters → UTF-8 bytes → <0xNN> token IDs

UnigramTokenizer is used automatically by FlanT5TextGenerator, CoeditGrammarCorrector, and T5SqlGenerator. It reads vocabulary and scores from tokenizer.json.

docs.title: Default behavior
docs.text:
You don't need to configure tokenizers for standard use. Every NLP wrapper auto-loads the correct tokenizer from the model directory during .build():

// WordPiece loaded automatically from vocab.txt
try (var classifier = DistilBertTextClassifier.builder()
        .modelId("inference4j/distilbert-base-uncased-finetuned-sst-2-english")
        .build()) {
    classifier.classify("This movie was fantastic!");
}

// BPE loaded automatically from vocab.json + merges.txt
try (var classifier = ClipClassifier.builder().build()) {
    classifier.classify(Path.of("photo.jpg"), List.of("cat", "dog", "bird"));
}

The wrapper knows which tokenizer algorithm its model expects and which vocabulary files to look for.

docs.title: Supplying a custom tokenizer
docs.text:
All NLP builders expose a .tokenizer() method that lets you override the default:

Tokenizer myTokenizer = WordPieceTokenizer.fromVocabFile(Path.of("/path/to/my/vocab.txt"));

try (var embedder = SentenceTransformerEmbedder.builder()
        .modelId("my-custom-model")
        .tokenizer(myTokenizer)
        .build()) {
    float[] embedding = embedder.encode("Hello, world!");
}

When you provide a tokenizer, the wrapper skips auto-loading and uses yours directly.

docs.title: When to use a custom tokenizer
docs.text:
Shared instances — if you're running multiple wrappers against the same vocabulary, share a single tokenizer instance to avoid loading the vocabulary file multiple times:

Tokenizer shared = WordPieceTokenizer.fromVocabFile(Path.of("vocab.txt"));

try (var embedder = SentenceTransformerEmbedder.builder()
            .modelId("my-model").tokenizer(shared).build();
     var classifier = DistilBertTextClassifier.builder()
            .modelId("my-model").tokenizer(shared).build()) {
    // Both use the same tokenizer instance
}

Custom vocabulary — if you've fine-tuned a model with a modified vocabulary, point the tokenizer at your custom vocab.txt:

Tokenizer tokenizer = WordPieceTokenizer.fromVocabFile(Path.of("my-custom-vocab.txt"));
try (var classifier = DistilBertTextClassifier.builder()
        .tokenizer(tokenizer)
        .modelSource(LocalModelSource.of(Path.of("my-finetuned-model")))
        .build()) {
    classifier.classify("custom domain text");
}

Testing — supply a mock or stub tokenizer in unit tests to isolate inference logic from tokenization:

Tokenizer stub = text -> new EncodedInput(
    new long[]{101, 7592, 102},
    new long[]{1, 1, 1},
    new long[]{0, 0, 0}
);

docs.title: The EncodedInput record
docs.text:
All tokenizers return an EncodedInput containing the three standard tensors that transformer models expect:

public record EncodedInput(
    long[] inputIds,       // token IDs from the vocabulary
    long[] attentionMask,  // 1 for real tokens, 0 for padding
    long[] tokenTypeIds    // segment IDs (0 for first sentence, 1 for second)
) {}
Field Purpose Example inputIds Maps each token to its vocabulary index [101, 7592, 2088, 102] attentionMask Tells the model which positions are real tokens vs padding [1, 1, 1, 1] tokenTypeIds Distinguishes sentence A from sentence B in pair tasks [0, 0, 0, 0]

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• You almost never need to touch tokenizers. The default auto-loading handles standard HuggingFace models out of the box.
  • Tokenizer and model must match. A tokenizer trained on one vocabulary will produce wrong token IDs for a model trained on a different vocabulary. Always use the tokenizer that shipped with your model.
  • maxLength matters. Most BERT models use 512 tokens max. CLIP uses 77. Exceeding the model's trained length produces undefined results. The wrappers set this automatically.
  • WordPiece does not pad, BPE does. WordPiece returns only the actual tokens (variable length). BPE pads to maxLength with zeros. Both behaviors match what their respective model families expect.

docs.title: inference4j for LangChain4j
docs.text: inference4j-langchain4j provides inference4j models as implementations of LangChain4j interfaces, for use in ingestion pipelines, retrievers and AI Services. The models run inside the JVM, without an API key, a model server or Python.

docs.title: Adapters
docs.text:
Use case Adapter LangChain4j interface Page Redact personal data from documents before they are embedded and stored Inference4jPiiRedactor DocumentTransformer, TextSegmentTransformer PII redaction Block prompt injection in user messages with a classifier Inference4jPromptInjectionGuardrail InputGuardrail Prompt-injection guardrail Read the text in scanned pages, screenshots and photos Inference4jOcrDocumentParser DocumentParser OCR document parser Transcribe recordings into documents with timestamps Inference4jAudioDocumentParser DocumentParser Audio document parser Embed text, with query and document prefixes applied from the input type Inference4jEmbeddingModel EmbeddingModel Embedding model Rerank retrieved content with a cross-encoder Inference4jScoringModel ScoringModel Reranking Run the LLM in-process: Phi-4-mini, Phi-3-mini, DeepSeek-R1, Qwen3, SmolLM3 Inference4jChatModel, Inference4jStreamingChatModel ChatModel, StreamingChatModel Chat model

RAG pipelines shows how the adapters fit together, with examples for recordings and scanned documents.

docs.title: Comparison with LangChain4j's built-in options
docs.text: Capability LangChain4j 1.23 inference4j adapter PII detection and redaction Not provided GLiNER PII model as a DocumentTransformer / TextSegmentTransformer Prompt-injection detection PatternBasedPromptInjectionGuardrail (regular expressions), DecisionModelInputGuardrail (one LLM call per message) DeBERTa-v3 classifier, about 10 ms per message on a laptop CPU OCR Docling parser (calls a separate docling-serve process), or a multimodal chat model PaddleOCR PP-OCRv6 in-process, about 31 MB of models Speech to documents AudioTranscriptionModel, implemented by hosted providers; responses carry no timestamps Moonshine, Whisper or Wav2Vec2 in-process, one Document per timed segment Local embeddings Packaged in-process ONNX models (all-MiniLM-L6-v2, bge-small, e5-small) and OnnxEmbeddingModel for a custom file bge-base, gte-base, nomic-embed-text-v1.5 (8K context, Matryoshka sizes); query/document prefixes from EmbeddingInputType Local reranking OnnxScoringModel, given paths to a model file and a tokenizer.json Cross-encoder downloaded and cached automatically; MaxP for long segments Local chat model Ollama (separate server), Jlama (in-process) and others onnxruntime-genai in-process, INT4 models downloaded and cached automatically; no tool calling

docs.title: Choosing an embedding or scoring model
docs.text:
Both libraries run embedding and reranking models in-process on ONNX Runtime.

LangChain4j in-process models inference4j adapters Model files Packaged in the jar (embeddings), or paths supplied by the caller (OnnxEmbeddingModel, OnnxScoringModel) Downloaded from HuggingFace on first use and cached Models all-MiniLM-L6-v2, bge-small-en, bge-small-zh, e5-small-v2, or a custom ONNX file The models listed under Embedding model and Reranking Query/document prefixes Added to the text by the caller Applied from EmbeddingInputType Batches Embedded in parallel on a thread pool Embedded one text at a time; each run uses all cores Long input Embeddings: split into partitions and averaged. Scoring: truncated Truncated by default; windows with .stride(int) (averaged for embeddings, MaxP for scoring)

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Add the adapter module next to the LangChain4j dependencies. It includes inference4j-core.

GradleMaven 
implementation 'io.github.inference4j:inference4j-langchain4j:${inference4jVersion}'
implementation 'dev.langchain4j:langchain4j:${langchain4jVersion}'

<dependency>
    <groupId>io.github.inference4j</groupId>
    <artifactId>inference4j-langchain4j</artifactId>
    <version>${inference4jVersion}</version>
</dependency>
<dependency>
    <groupId>dev.langchain4j</groupId>
    <artifactId>langchain4j</artifactId>
    <version>${langchain4jVersion}</version>
</dependency>
inference4j 0.14.0 or later LangChain4j 1.23.0 (tested) Java 17 or later
  • LangChain4j is a compileOnly dependency of the module. The application supplies its own LangChain4j version.
  • ONNX Runtime requires the JVM flag --enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED. See Installation.
  • The chat model adapters and WhisperSpeechModel require inference4j-genai. All other models on these pages are in inference4j-core.

Experimental LangChain4j APIs

LangChain4j marks guardrails and the embedding request API (EmbeddingInputType) as experimental. They may change in a later LangChain4j release.

ONNX Runtime version

inference4j requires ONNX Runtime 1.28.0. LangChain4j's in-process modules (langchain4j-embeddings-*, langchain4j-onnx-scoring, and langchain4j-easy-rag, which includes an embedding module) declare ONNX Runtime 1.23.2. When both are on the classpath, make sure the build resolves 1.28.0: Gradle selects the newer version, Maven selects the version declared closest to the project. LangChain4j's ONNX modules are not tested with 1.28.0.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
A retrieval-augmented assistant with a local embedding model and a local guardrail. The chat model can be any LangChain4j ChatModel:

import dev.langchain4j.data.document.Document;
import dev.langchain4j.data.document.splitter.DocumentSplitters;
import dev.langchain4j.data.segment.TextSegment;
import dev.langchain4j.model.chat.ChatModel;
import dev.langchain4j.rag.content.retriever.EmbeddingStoreContentRetriever;
import dev.langchain4j.service.AiServices;
import dev.langchain4j.store.embedding.EmbeddingStoreIngestor;
import dev.langchain4j.store.embedding.inmemory.InMemoryEmbeddingStore;
import io.github.inference4j.langchain4j.Inference4jEmbeddingModel;
import io.github.inference4j.langchain4j.Inference4jPromptInjectionGuardrail;
import io.github.inference4j.nlp.DebertaPromptInjectionDetector;
import io.github.inference4j.nlp.SentenceTransformerEmbedder;

interface Assistant {
    String chat(String message);
}

ChatModel chatModel = ...;          // any LangChain4j chat model, or Inference4jChatModel
List<Document> documents = ...;     // loaded with any LangChain4j document loader

var embeddingModel = Inference4jEmbeddingModel.builder()
        .embedder(SentenceTransformerEmbedder.builder()
                .modelId("inference4j/all-MiniLM-L6-v2").normalize().build())
        .build();

var store = new InMemoryEmbeddingStore<TextSegment>();
EmbeddingStoreIngestor.builder()
        .documentSplitter(DocumentSplitters.recursive(300, 30))
        .embeddingModel(embeddingModel)
        .embeddingStore(store)
        .build()
        .ingest(documents);

Assistant assistant = AiServices.builder(Assistant.class)
        .chatModel(chatModel)
        .contentRetriever(EmbeddingStoreContentRetriever.builder()
                .embeddingStore(store).embeddingModel(embeddingModel).maxResults(4).build())
        .inputGuardrails(new Inference4jPromptInjectionGuardrail(
                DebertaPromptInjectionDetector.builder().build()))
        .build();

assistant.chat("What is the cancellation policy?");

Models are downloaded from HuggingFace on first use and cached under ~/.cache/inference4j. See Model loading for offline use and custom locations.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
Closing an adapter closes its model

Each adapter owns the inference4j model passed to it. close() on the adapter closes that model and frees its native memory.

  • Give each adapter its own model instance. A model wrapped in two adapters is closed when either adapter is closed.
  • Calls on a closed model throw IllegalStateException.
  • Close adapters on application shutdown. All adapters are AutoCloseable.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Scanned PDFs. The OCR parser reads images. PDF pages must be rasterized first; see OCR document parser.
  • Chat messages. The PII redactor implements the ingestion interfaces only. See PII redaction.
  • Compressed audio and video. The audio parser reads WAV.
  • Tool calling. The chat model adapters do not support tools. See Chat model.

docs.title: Audio document parser
docs.text: Inference4jAudioDocumentParser is a LangChain4j DocumentParser that turns a recording into text documents with inference4j speech-to-text, in-process. Segments carry their start and end time in the recording.

docs.title: Quick example
docs.text:
try (var parser = new Inference4jAudioDocumentParser(new SegmentedSpeechRecognizer(
        MoonshineRecognizer.builder().build(),
        SileroVadDetector.builder().build()))) {

    // One document with the whole transcript
    Document transcript = FileSystemDocumentLoader.loadDocument(Path.of("meeting.wav"), parser);

    // One document per timed segment
    try (InputStream in = Files.newInputStream(Path.of("meeting.wav"))) {
        List<Document> segments = parser.parseSegments(in);
    }
}

SegmentedSpeechRecognizer cuts long recordings at pauses and produces the timed segments. Whisper requires it for audio longer than 30 seconds.

docs.title: Two ways to parse
Merging short segments
docs.text:
Pieces of a few seconds often hold too little text to match a question. mergeSegments(int) on the builder joins consecutive segments into documents of up to that many characters:

var parser = Inference4jAudioDocumentParser.builder()
        .recognizer(new SegmentedSpeechRecognizer(
                MoonshineRecognizer.builder().build(),
                SileroVadDetector.builder().build(),
                Duration.ofSeconds(8)))
        .mergeSegments(300)
        .build();

A merged document has the start_ms of its first segment and the end_ms of its last, so it still points to where it starts in the recording. segment_index counts the merged documents. A single segment longer than the limit stays whole. Short segments with merging keep answers close to the moment they came from; long segments lose that precision.

Builder option Default Description .recognizer(SpeechRecognizer) — (required) The recognizer, typically a SegmentedSpeechRecognizer; closed by the parser .mergeSegments(int) off Join consecutive segments from parseSegments into documents of up to this many characters

The constructor new Inference4jAudioDocumentParser(recognizer) is the same as the builder without merging.

docs.title: Segment metadata
Choosing a recognizer
docs.text:
The parser has one constructor, Inference4jAudioDocumentParser(SpeechRecognizer), and accepts any inference4j recognizer.

Recognizer Module Size Output Notes MoonshineRecognizer inference4j-core ~140 MB (small, default) Punctuated, cased English WhisperSpeechModel inference4j-genai ~225 MB (tiny) to ~1.1 GB (small) Punctuated, cased 99 languages; must be wrapped in SegmentedSpeechRecognizer for audio over 30 seconds Wav2Vec2Recognizer inference4j-core ~370 MB Upper-case, no punctuation English. Combine with PunctuatedSpeechRecognizer to restore punctuation and casing 
// Wav2Vec2 with punctuation restored, cut at pauses
var parser = new Inference4jAudioDocumentParser(new SegmentedSpeechRecognizer(
        new PunctuatedSpeechRecognizer(
                Wav2Vec2Recognizer.builder().build(),
                PunctCapSegModel.builder().build()),
        SileroVadDetector.builder().build()));

Segment length is set on SegmentedSpeechRecognizer: pieces end at pauses and are at most 30 seconds by default. Pass a Duration as the third constructor argument for shorter segments. See Long recordings.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• WAV only. Input must be WAV (8- or 16-bit PCM, mono or stereo, any sample rate). Convert MP3, M4A and video first, for example ffmpeg -i talk.mp4 -ac 1 -ar 16000 talk.wav. Other input fails with InferenceException.
  • Silence. parse throws InferenceException ("No speech detected in audio") because LangChain4j documents cannot be blank. parseSegments returns an empty list.
  • Segment boundaries. A segment spans one piece of audio between pauses, including up to half a pause of silence at each end. There is no speaker identification.
  • Without SegmentedSpeechRecognizer, parseSegments returns a single document spanning the whole recording.
  • Memory and disk. The stream is copied to a temporary file, which is deleted afterwards, and the decoded audio is held in memory while it is transcribed.
  • Lifecycle. close() closes the recognizer and, through SegmentedSpeechRecognizer, the models it wraps. See Lifecycle.

inference4j does not implement LangChain4j's AudioTranscriptionModel interface, whose response carries text without timestamps.

docs.title: Chat model
docs.text: Inference4jChatModel and Inference4jStreamingChatModel are a LangChain4j ChatModel and StreamingChatModel backed by an inference4j TextGenerator. The LLM runs inside the JVM through onnxruntime-genai, without an API key or a model server.

docs.title: Quick example
docs.text:
var chatModel = new Inference4jChatModel(TextGenerator.builder()
        .model(ModelSources.phi4Mini())
        .maxNewTokens(300)
        .temperature(0)
        .build());

String answer = chatModel.chat("What is the capital of France?");

Phi-4-mini (about 4.9 GB) is downloaded on first use.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
The chat model adapters need inference4j-genai next to inference4j-langchain4j. The other adapters do not.

GradleMaven 
implementation 'io.github.inference4j:inference4j-langchain4j:${inference4jVersion}'
implementation 'io.github.inference4j:inference4j-genai:${inference4jVersion}'
implementation 'dev.langchain4j:langchain4j:${langchain4jVersion}'

<dependency>
    <groupId>io.github.inference4j</groupId>
    <artifactId>inference4j-langchain4j</artifactId>
    <version>${inference4jVersion}</version>
</dependency>
<dependency>
    <groupId>io.github.inference4j</groupId>
    <artifactId>inference4j-genai</artifactId>
    <version>${inference4jVersion}</version>
</dependency>
<dependency>
    <groupId>dev.langchain4j</groupId>
    <artifactId>langchain4j</artifactId>
    <version>${langchain4jVersion}</version>
</dependency>

docs.title: With AI Services
docs.text:
interface Assistant {
    @SystemMessage("You are a support assistant. Answer in one or two sentences.")
    String chat(String message);
}

Assistant assistant = AiServices.builder(Assistant.class)
        .chatModel(chatModel)
        .chatMemory(MessageWindowChatMemory.withMaxMessages(10))
        .build();

System messages, chat memory and retrieved content all reach the model: the whole conversation is formatted with the model's chat template on every call.

docs.title: Streaming
docs.text:
interface StreamingAssistant {
    TokenStream chat(String message);
}

var streamingModel = new Inference4jStreamingChatModel(TextGenerator.builder()
        .model(ModelSources.phi4Mini())
        .maxNewTokens(300)
        .build());

StreamingAssistant assistant = AiServices.builder(StreamingAssistant.class)
        .streamingChatModel(streamingModel)
        .build();

assistant.chat("Name three Java build tools.")
        .onPartialResponse(System.out::print)
        .onCompleteResponse(response -> System.out.println())
        .onError(Throwable::printStackTrace)
        .start();

Generation runs on the calling thread: the handler receives every partial response, then the complete response or the error, before chat returns.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Each adapter has one constructor, taking a TextGenerator. Sampling and limits are set on the generator; see its builder options.

Generator option Description .model(GenerativeModel) A model from ModelSources: Phi-3-mini, Phi-4-mini, DeepSeek-R1, Qwen3, SmolLM3 .maxNewTokens(int) Maximum length of each answer .maxLength(int) Tokens for the whole conversation plus the answer; sizes the key/value cache .temperature(double) 0 for greedy decoding, the same answer for the same input .stopSequence(String) Ends the answer when the string appears .intraOpThreads(int) Threads per ONNX Runtime session

docs.title: Response
docs.text: Field Value aiMessage().text() The generated text tokenUsage() Prompt tokens, after the chat template is applied, and generated tokens finishReason() LENGTH when maxNewTokens or maxLength was reached, STOP otherwise

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Chat templates. The conversation is formatted with the generator's ChatTemplate. The models in ModelSources have templates that format whole conversations. A custom model needs a template that implements format(List<ChatMessage>); see Chat templates.
  • No tool calling. A request with tool specifications, or a conversation with tool calls, throws UnsupportedOperationException. The streaming adapter reports it to onError.
  • No per-request sampling. A request that sets temperature, top-p, top-k, maximum output tokens, stop sequences or penalties is rejected. Set them on the generator.
  • Text only. Images and other non-text content are rejected; a JSON response format is rejected.
  • One call at a time. The generator runs one generation at a time and queues the others, because each generation reserves a key/value cache for maxLength tokens. For parallel generation, create one adapter per generator.
  • Small models. Models of a few billion parameters answer focused questions from the given context well. They are less reliable at combining facts from several sources or following long instructions.
  • Lifecycle. close() closes the generator. See Lifecycle.

docs.title: Embedding model
docs.text: Inference4jEmbeddingModel is a LangChain4j EmbeddingModel backed by an inference4j SentenceTransformerEmbedder, running in-process. Use it anywhere LangChain4j takes an EmbeddingModel: EmbeddingStoreIngestor, EmbeddingStoreContentRetriever, or directly.

docs.title: Quick example
docs.text:
var embeddingModel = Inference4jEmbeddingModel.builder()
        .embedder(SentenceTransformerEmbedder.builder()
                .modelId("inference4j/all-MiniLM-L6-v2").normalize().build())
        .build();

Response<Embedding> embedding = embeddingModel.embed("Hello, world!");
int dimension = embeddingModel.dimension();     // 384

docs.title: Query and document prefixes
docs.text:
Retrieval models such as nomic-embed, E5 and BGE are trained with one prefix on queries and another on documents. A missing or wrong prefix lowers retrieval quality without raising an error.

The adapter reads LangChain4j's EmbeddingInputType from each request and applies the matching prefix, so one model instance serves both ingestion and retrieval:

var embeddingModel = Inference4jEmbeddingModel.builder()
        .embedder(SentenceTransformerEmbedder.builder()
                .modelId("inference4j/nomic-embed-text-v1.5").normalize().build())
        .queryPrefix("search_query: ")
        .documentPrefix("search_document: ")
        .build();

EmbeddingStoreIngestor.builder()
        .embeddingModel(embeddingModel)
        .embeddingStore(store)
        .embeddingInputType(EmbeddingInputType.DOCUMENT)      // "search_document: " + segment
        .build()
        .ingest(documents);

ContentRetriever retriever = EmbeddingStoreContentRetriever.builder()
        .embeddingModel(embeddingModel)
        .embeddingStore(store)
        .embeddingInputType(EmbeddingInputType.QUERY)         // "search_query: " + question
        .build();

Set embeddingInputType on both the ingestor and the retriever

LangChain4j sends no input type unless one is set. A request without one is embedded as the adapter's defaultInputType (DOCUMENT unless changed), so a retriever without embeddingInputType(QUERY) embeds questions with the document prefix. The first such request logs a warning when a prefix is configured.

Either prefix can be left unset. BGE, for example, only puts an instruction on queries:

var embeddingModel = Inference4jEmbeddingModel.builder()
        .embedder(SentenceTransformerEmbedder.builder()
                .modelId("inference4j/bge-base-en-v1.5")
                .poolingStrategy(PoolingStrategy.CLS).normalize().build())
        .queryPrefix("Represent this sentence for searching relevant passages: ")
        .build();

docs.title: Builder options
docs.text:
Method Type Default Description .embedder(SentenceTransformerEmbedder) SentenceTransformerEmbedder — (required) The model to run. Build it without .textPrefix(...); the adapter's prefixes replace it on every call .queryPrefix(String) String none Prefix for QUERY inputs, e.g. "search_query: " (nomic) or "query: " (E5) .documentPrefix(String) String none Prefix for DOCUMENT inputs, e.g. "search_document: " (nomic) or "passage: " (E5) .defaultInputType(EmbeddingInputType) EmbeddingInputType DOCUMENT Input type for requests that carry none .dimension(int) int probed Size reported by dimension(). Without it, the adapter embeds one short text the first time dimension() is called. Must match the embedder's output, including its Matryoshka .dimensions(int) .modelName(String) String LangChain4j's default Name reported by modelName() and in response metadata

Model settings (pooling, normalization, maximum length, long-input windows, Matryoshka size, hardware acceleration) are set on the embedder. See its builder options.

docs.title: Model choices
docs.text:
Model ID Dimensions Size Prefixes Notes inference4j/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 384 ~90 MB none Also packaged by LangChain4j as AllMiniLmL6V2EmbeddingModel inference4j/bge-base-en-v1.5 768 ~430 MB query only Use PoolingStrategy.CLS inference4j/gte-base 768 ~430 MB none inference4j/nomic-embed-text-v1.5 768, or 512 / 256 / 128 / 64 ~520 MB search_query: / search_document: Reads up to 8,192 tokens with .maxLength(8192); Matryoshka sizes with .dimensions(int)

More models and their settings are listed under Semantic search and Supported models.

docs.title: Smaller vectors (Matryoshka)
docs.text:
nomic-embed-text-v1.5 vectors can be shortened with little loss, which reduces index size and search time. Set the size on the embedder and on the adapter:

var embeddingModel = Inference4jEmbeddingModel.builder()
        .embedder(SentenceTransformerEmbedder.builder()
                .modelId("inference4j/nomic-embed-text-v1.5").normalize().dimensions(256).build())
        .queryPrefix("search_query: ")
        .documentPrefix("search_document: ")
        .dimension(256)
        .build();

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Normalize. Build the embedder with .normalize() when the embedding store compares by cosine similarity.
  • Per-call dimensions and modelName are rejected. The only request parameter the adapter supports is inputType; LangChain4j fails a request that sets any other with UnsupportedFeatureException.
  • Batches run sequentially. embedAll embeds one input at a time; each run uses all cores. See Choosing an embedding or scoring model.
  • Long segments. Text over the embedder's maxLength (512 tokens by default) is truncated with a warning. Split documents into segments that fit, or set .stride(int) on the embedder to average windows; with stride, the prefix is repeated in every window.
  • Token usage is not reported. EmbeddingResponse carries embeddings and the model name only.
  • Lifecycle. close() closes the embedder. See Lifecycle.

docs.title: OCR document parser
docs.text: Inference4jOcrDocumentParser is a LangChain4j DocumentParser that reads the text in an image with inference4j OCR (PaddleOCR PP-OCRv6), in-process. The default models are about 31 MB.

docs.title: Quick example
docs.text:
try (var parser = new Inference4jOcrDocumentParser(OcrPipeline.builder().build())) {
    Document invoice = FileSystemDocumentLoader.loadDocument(Path.of("invoice.png"), parser);
    System.out.println(invoice.text());
}

The parser works with any LangChain4j document loader. To load a directory of images:

PathMatcher images = FileSystems.getDefault().getPathMatcher("glob:*.{png,jpg,jpeg}");
List<Document> scans = FileSystemDocumentLoader.loadDocuments(Path.of("scans"), images, parser);

loadDocuments skips files that fail to parse, such as an image without text, and logs a warning.

docs.title: What the document contains
docs.text:
• Text: one line per detected line of text, top to bottom, then left to right.
  • Metadata: the loader's own keys (such as file_name), plus:
Key Type Value ocr_line_count (Inference4jOcrDocumentParser.LINE_COUNT) int Number of text lines read ocr_mean_confidence (Inference4jOcrDocumentParser.MEAN_CONFIDENCE) double Mean recognition confidence of those lines, 0 to 1

The confidence can be used to filter low-quality scans:

Document scan = FileSystemDocumentLoader.loadDocument(path, parser);
if (scan.metadata().getDouble(Inference4jOcrDocumentParser.MEAN_CONFIDENCE) < 0.8) {
    // skip, or route to manual review
}

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
The parser has one constructor, Inference4jOcrDocumentParser(OcrPipeline). Options are set on the pipeline:

Pipeline option Default Description .minConfidence(float) 0 (keep every line) Drop lines read with a lower confidence .detector(TextDetector) PaddleTextDetector.small() Finds the lines .recognizer(TextRecognizer) PaddleTextRecognizer.small() Reads each line 
var parser = new Inference4jOcrDocumentParser(OcrPipeline.builder()
        .detector(PaddleTextDetector.tiny().build())        // ~6 MB in total, a little less accurate
        .recognizer(PaddleTextRecognizer.tiny().build())
        .minConfidence(0.5f)
        .build());

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Image formats. Anything javax.imageio.ImageIO reads: PNG, JPEG, BMP and GIF with a standard JDK. Other input fails with InferenceException ("Unsupported image format").
  • Images without text. LangChain4j documents cannot be blank, so an image without text throws InferenceException ("No text found in image").
  • Layout. Lines are ordered by position only. Multi-column pages and tables are read row by row, and table and heading structure is not preserved. LangChain4j's Docling parser provides layout-aware conversion.
  • Scripts. The default recognizer's dictionary covers Latin scripts, Chinese and Japanese. See OCR.
  • Lifecycle. close() closes the pipeline, including its detector and recognizer. See Lifecycle.

docs.title: Scanned PDFs
docs.text:
The parser reads images, not PDFs. Render each page to an image first, for example with Apache PDFBox 3, and parse each page:

List<Document> pages = new ArrayList<>();
try (PDDocument pdf = Loader.loadPDF(new File("contract.pdf"))) {
    PDFRenderer renderer = new PDFRenderer(pdf);
    for (int page = 0; page < pdf.getNumberOfPages(); page++) {
        BufferedImage image = renderer.renderImageWithDPI(page, 200);

        ByteArrayOutputStream png = new ByteArrayOutputStream();
        ImageIO.write(image, "png", png);
        try {
            Document document = parser.parse(new ByteArrayInputStream(png.toByteArray()));
            document.metadata().put("file_name", "contract.pdf").put("page", page + 1);
            pages.add(document);
        } catch (InferenceException e) {
            // a page without text
        }
    }
}

For PDFs with a text layer, use LangChain4j's ApachePdfBoxDocumentParser, which extracts the text directly.

docs.title: Other OCR options
docs.text: Option Runs Output Inference4jOcrDocumentParser In the JVM Lines of plain text from an image LangChain4j Docling parser A separate docling-serve process Structured documents with layout and tables, from many file formats A multimodal chat model Hosted API, or a local model server Model-generated text; one model call per image

docs.title: PII redaction
